findings.body: The raw StatusContext nodes retain `createdAt`, but `_green_at` reads only `completedAt` or `startedAt` (src/forge/board.py:515–524). GitHub CLI previously mapped a status's creation time to `startedAt` in its [JSON exporter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cli/cli/trunk/api/export_pr.go). For an item waiting for checks whose required checks are successful commit statuses, the JSON board therefore reports checks `pass` while its next step remains `forge close <item>` instead of the merge instruction. The HTML board also stops recognizing that PR as ready because it now consumes this same rollup. Normalize StatusContext timestamps for these consumers and preserve the CheckRun start-time fallback.
findings.title: Preserve commit-status timestamps when adapting the GraphQL rollup

findings.body: Detail 1 explicitly assigns VIEWS a command test containing all four together, including GitHub-unreachable behavior. This test creates a story and running task worker but no fix; the fix assertions in tests 2 and 3 use separate repositories without a story. The client lifecycle test selects only the story row and does not assert a running worker. Consequently, the suite would still pass if story presence suppressed fix rows. Extend the command scenario to assert both root rows, the running worker, PR checks, and retained rows with unknown checks when GitHub is unreachable.
findings.title: Not done: board command coverage with a story, fix, running worker and open pull request

findings.body: This marks every SKIPPED or NEUTRAL check as passed, even when its name matches a required check. Forge's existing gate treats both conclusions as failed for named checks (src/forge/checks.py:35–38 and 68–70), including matrix variants. The machine board can therefore show checks `pass` with no failure occurrence while `forge close` refuses the same PR. Apply the required-name rule when classifying these conclusions; optional skipped or neutral checks can remain passed.
findings.title: Keep skipped required checks from appearing green
